top.title: Own goal helps Brighton & Hove Albion record victory at Everton
top.description: Own goal helps Brighton & Hove Albion record victory at Everton A Maz Pacheco own goal helped Brighton & Hove Albion to record a 1-0 victory over Everton at Goodison Park on Sunday afternoon. Pacheco put through her own net after just six minutes as the visitors ended the second block of matches with a win. Olivia García created an early chance for Brighton & Hove Albion. She passed the ball to captain Maisie Symonds, but she sent her effort wide. Pacheco then netted an own goal when her back-pass deceived both Rion Ishikawa and Courtney Brosnan and the ball rolled into the goal. Brighton & Hove Albion searched for a second goal. A ball was played through by Lily Murphy towards Kiko Seike, but her touch wasn’t enough and it was caught well by Brosnan. Fran Kirby then played the ball to Seike, but Ishikawa timed her run perfectly and intercepted the ball. Ornella Vignola almost found an equaliser for Everton. She attempted to whip the ball towards the far corner, but her shot went just wide. Hannah Blundell was then in on goal, but her shot was saved by Chiamaka Nnadozie. Jutta Rantala was next to have a chance in the box, but her effort was blocked. Brighton & Hove Albion went close when Marisa Olislagers struck the ball from range, but Brosnan got her finger tips to it as the game ended 1-0 in The Seagulls’ favour. This afternoon’s result sees Brighton & Hove Albion go to seventh place in the Barclays Women’s Super League table while Everton drop to 11th.

top.title: Bremen thrash Hamburg in derby, Augsburg win with Gregoritsch's brace
top.description: Hamburg's Miro Muheim battles for the ball with Werder Bremen's Ludovit Reis during German Bundesliga soccer match between Werder Bremen and Hamburger SV at the Weserstadion. (is associated with: «Bremen thrash Hamburg in derby, Augsburg win with Gregoritsch's brace») Carmen Jaspersen/dpa Werder Bremen lit up in the second half, with Justin Njinmah scoring a brace, to thrash Hamburg 4-0 in the Bundesliga Northern derby on Sunday. After a goalless first half, Bremen captain Marco Friedl broke the deadlock in the 55th minute. Goalkeeper Daniel Heuer Fernandes parried his first effort after a corner, but the ball returned to the skipper, who didn't miss the second chance and hit a powerful volley into the net. Njinmah then found the net twice, in the 66th and then in 70th, before fan favourite Niclas Füllkrug sealed the victory with a stunner in stoppage time. "Clear derby win, 4-0. We can all go back home happy today," Njinmah told broadcasters DAZN. Bremen, who finished the previous season just three points above the relegation zone, are having a good campaign so far and are sixth in the table, while Hamburg are 12th. Earlier, Michael Gregoritsch also scored a brace to lead Augsburg to a 3-1 win against Mainz. The Austrian forward broke the deadlock for the hosts in the 19th minute. Yannik Keitel's effort from a corner was kept out by goalkeeper Robin Zentner, but Gregoritsch poked the rebound home. Juma Bah made it 2-0 in the 36th from a similar situation. Zentner again stopped the initial attempt after a corner, but the loose ball fell to Bah, who fired it into the net. Keitel thought he had a third, but the goal was ruled out due to a foul. Augsburg coach Manuel Baum was frustrated with the decision and had a confrontation with Nadiem Amiri as he refused to return the ball. Baum was sent off, while Amiri received a yellow card. The incident didn't seem to affect the Augsburg players and Gregoritsch scored another goal early in the second half. A free-kick was initially cleared by the Mainz defence, but the ball was returned to the area. It looped in the air before bouncing off the back of Stefan Posch's head and into the path of Gregoritsch, who volleyed it home in the 48th. Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer pulled one back for Mainz three minutes later but couldn't threaten a comeback. Augsburg moved up to 10th, while Mainz dropped to 13th. "Today we not only defended well, but also played really well with the ball. Especially with the unfamiliar defensive line-up, the team handled it brilliantly – a huge compliment to them," Baum said. Bayern Munich were held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne on Friday, which opened the door for Borussia Dortmund to take the Bundesliga lead after a 1-0 win against Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday. top.title: Manchester United humbled at Liverpool on Pochettino’s debut as boss
top.description: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Manchester United at the Anfield. (is associated with: «Manchester United humbled at Liverpool on Pochettino’s debut as boss») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United reign got off to a miserable start as Liverpool punished Leny Yoro’s red card with a pair of early goals on their way to a comprehensive 4-0 win against their relegation-threatened rivals. A whirlwind week for the former Argentina international ended in all too familiar disappointment for the faltering Red Devils, whose hopes of enjoying a new manager bounce were extinguished within 13 nightmare minutes at Anfield. Dominik Szoboszlai’s fierce free-kick put Liverpool ahead after United defender Yoro was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity and Florian Wirtz’s smart finish quickly put Pochettino’s side further behind. United temporarily stemmed the tide thanks to some last-ditch defending, wayward finishing and key Senne Lammens stops, but Andoni Iraola’s Reds redoubled their efforts in the second half. In truth, Pochettino’s 10 men were fortunate that Liverpool only added a further two goals though Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz, such was their dominance. Iraola’s side end the weekend in fourth whereas United languish 19th in the standings as their winless Premier League run stretched to a ninth match and attention now turns to Wednesday’s Champions League trip to Sporting.

top.title: Baltimore Ravens’ Other Trade Offer for Former First-Round QB Revealed
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens’ season went off the rails when Lamar Jackson suffered a dislocated thumb on his right hand, knocking him out for an extended stretch, if not the rest of the year. The Ravens’ general manager Eric DeCosta responded by trading for 11-year veteran Jacoby Brissett. While the Ravens have a new quarterback who they feel is more capable of leading a winning effort, he wasn’t their first choice once Jackson got hurt. Baltimore also tried trading for a different quarterback first, but their negotiations got shut down. Still, who were the Ravens looking to add to the roster? Baltimore Ravens Tried Trading Fourth-Round Pick for Daniel Jones Nov 19, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) looks on from the sideline during the game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images While the Ravens are moving forward with Brissett, according to multiple sources, they also attempted to negotiate a trade with the Indianapolis Colts for Daniel Jones before the Nov. 10 trade deadline expired. The Ravens weren’t the only team to try trading for the former first-round pick, the Minnesota Vikings were reportedly involved too. Yet, the Colts surprised everyone by telling teams that Jones was off-limits in trade discussions. That was a curious decision, considering the Colts released him from the roster 10 days later. Now, according to ESPN’s top NFL insider Adam Schefter , the Ravens offered a fourth-round pick in exchange for Jones and a fifth-round pick. But the trade was conditional. If the Ravens made the playoffs, they’d be sending that fifth-round pick back to the Colts. Nevertheless, the Colts didn’t want to play ball, and they held onto Jones through the deadline before later cutting him loose. “The Ravens offered the Colts a fourth-round draft pick for Daniel Jones and a fifth-round pick, with the condition that the fifth-rounder would be returned to Indianapolis if Baltimore advanced to the playoffs. Minnesota also had interest in Jones. Indy held him, then released him.” Adam Schefter on Daniel Jones Trade Jones is a free agent right now, so if the Ravens are still interested, there’s a chance he could still end up in Baltimore. Yet now that they picked Brissett as the starter, odds are the former No. 6 overall pick will end up elsewhere. Still just 29 years old, there will likely be several teams interested in seeing if they can help get Jones back on track after tossing an NFL-high 13 interceptions thus far. While he likely isn’t looking at another starting role right away, Jones could latch onto a practice squad for the remainder of the season again, much like he did two years ago by joining Kevin O’Connell’s staff in Minnesota. top.title: Roy Keane slams Man Utd fans for applauding players after Liverpool defeat
top.description: Roy Keane slams Man Utd fans for applauding players after Liverpool defeat Roy Keane has hit out at the Manchester United fans applauding the side’s effort in defeat to Liverpool. Manchester United began the Mauricio Pochettino era with a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield. A nightmare start saw United reduced to 10 men inside eight minutes when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Liverpool ruthlessly punished the visitors with quick-fire goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz. Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz added further goals after the interval, as the home side secured an emphatic win. The result piles the pressure on Manchester United, who remain in the Premier League’s relegation places with one win from 11 games. Though large numbers of travelling fans departed Anfield before full-time, Keane questioned the supporters who remained to applaud the side’s effort with 10 men. The former Manchester United captain was confused by any credit for an unacceptable performance. “Has a team ever got a result before with 10 men? It can be done,” Keane said to Sky Sports. “Are you telling me Man Utd couldn’t have done better and everyone is saying it’s not bad. “At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality, I can’t believe what I’m hearing. Fans are applauding the players, applauding what? Applauding rubbish. “When do the players take responsibility for some of the decision making? Liverpool should have scored eight or nine. I feel like swearing. How can anyone say 4-0 is not too bad? top.title: Hornets Considering Paying Too High A Price For Zion Williamson Trade
top.description: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets sit at 4-11 and need a spark, but a proposed trade for Zion Williamson looks like a terrible mistake. The team is desperate for offense after a 111-97 loss in Atlanta on Friday night, yet the cost to get the Pelicans star is simply too high. The Cost of Four Draft Picks The front office pitched the LaMelo deal as a move toward the future, yet this new proposal burns that future for a player with a shaky track record. Yahoo Sports reports that a complete cost analysis indicates paying such a price makes very little sense. Health Concerns and Salary Traps Availability remains the single biggest question mark for any team acquiring the 26-year-old forward. The risk remains massive even though clauses based on games played protect his $42.17 million salary for this season and his $44.89 million deal for 2027-28. Over the course of seven seasons, Williamson has played over just 60 games on only three occasions. The consensus is that he is unable to stay healthy. A Better Path Exists While Bleacher Report suggests “Zion Williamson would give the Hornets a similarly different offensive access point without creating redundancies with any of their core players,” the financial and asset cost is too steep. On the Hoop Collective podcast, ESPN’s Tim MacMahon reported that the Pelicans are unlikely to receive a blockbuster price. “And kind of the consensus that I’ve gotten is, hey, there will be interest in Zion, but there’s not going to be like a blockbuster type of return,” McMahon said. The Hornets should look elsewhere for stability rather than betting the farm on a player who cannot stay on the court.

top.title: Michigan Takes Down UCLA, Ready for Ohio State
top.description: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham reacts to a play against UCLA during the second half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Michigan football finally found its footing after a hard-fought win over UCLA . The Wolverines secured a spot in a bowl game with an 18-16 victory in triple overtime. This win at The Big House improved the team’s record to 6-5. But head coach Kyle Whittingham is not looking back at the celebration. His mind is already fixed on the next big challenge. The coaching staff knows the season is far from over. There is only one regular-season game left on the schedule. That final matchup is the annual rivalry against Ohio State. Whittingham knows the stakes are high as the team heads to Columbus. He wants his players to carry the momentum from Saturday forward. Facing a Hostile Road Trip Whittingham has never played inside Ohio Stadium, known as The Shoe. He admits he cannot fully picture the noise until he gets there. “I can envision it. I’ve never been in the Shoe, never played in that stadium,” Whittingham said. Whittingham has faced Ohio State before in a major bowl game. His Utah team met the Buckeyes in the 2022 Rose Bowl, losing a 48-45 shootout. “We did play Ohio State in the Rose Bowl 5 years ago, 4 years ago, so we’ve had a taste of that, and they were … we know they’re a very good football team, very talented,” he added. The coach expects the crowd in Columbus to be loud and angry. He mentioned that Ohio State lost a recent game in Nebraska. “I guess they got beat today in Nebraska, but I think the environment I’m anticipating to be very hostile,” he said. Whittingham has faced tough crowds in his long career. He is not sure if this one will be the worst he has seen, but he is ready to find out. The team must handle the pressure without breaking. Questions About the Coach’s Future While the team celebrates a bowl berth, some fans worry about Whittingham’s job. The season started with high hopes and a roster full of talent. Instead, the team struggled to find a rhythm for most of the year. Insiders at The Athletic reported that some parents of players may have mixed emotions; one said he can “get the program on track if given enough time.” Critics point to specific issues that hurt the team this year. According to The Athletic’s Bruce Feldman and Austin Meek, the offense utilized a “scheme that wasn’t built for the Big Ten.” They also noted a “CEO-style” approach that kept Whittingham too far from the field. Dan Wetzel on the Paul Finebaum Show argued that Whittingham’s legacy is safe despite this year. “Kyle Whittingham as a coach, his legacy is mostly secured. This just, for whatever reason, didn’t gel,” Wetzel stated. The final test will come next week in Ohio. Michigan heads to Columbus for its annual rivalry matchup against Ohio State on November 28. The Wolverines will look to carry the momentum from their win over UCLA into one of the season’s biggest challenges.

top.title: Israel Adesanya’s pre-UFC Saudi Arabia comments called ‘the most concerning interview I’ve ever seen’
top.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC Chael Sonnen hopes that Israel Adesanya can prove him wrong but has his doubts. On December 5, Israel Adesanya returns in the main event of UFC Saudi Arabia to try and break his four-fight losing streak. Sonnen recently commented on what the former two-time middleweight champion has had to say about how he plans on turning this form around when facing off with Shara Magomedov. Chael Sonnen is rooting for Israel Adesanya but is not convinced by his introspection In a video on his YouTube channel , Israel Adesanya said that he believes he’s been going wrong by trying to prove a point in his fights instead of utilising his best weapon, his mind. This mental shift and leaving his long-time home of City Kickboxing are two changes that ‘The Last Stylebender’ has implemented ahead of his return. Chael Sonnen argued in a video responding to Adesanya’s comments that you can’t think your way to success. He argued that countless fighters have made similar comments in the past but regardless of what changes you make, none of it can replace the hard work required to compete at the highest level. “I’ve seen interviews like this,” he said via his YouTube channel . “I’ve seen a guy that knows he knows the secret. The secret is the mind and he’s re-found himself. I’ve seen these interviews. “I’ve never seen it work out and I will tell you sincerely, I hope for the first time in history it works out and it works out for Izzy. I am a fan, but this interview is easily the most concerning interview that I’ve ever seen.” Sonnen agreed that Adesanya’s fight IQ is a big advantage that he brings to the table. He said that the amount of success the 37-year-old has achieved shows that he’s “the smartest guy in the gym”. With that in mind, Sonnen believes that regardless of Adesanya changing teams, getting back in the win column is something that’s on him. top.title: Pochettino era off to the worst start as new boss makes major blunder that condemns Man United to heavy loss vs Liverpool
top.description: Pochettino era off to the worst start as new boss makes major blunder that condemns Man United to heavy loss vs Liverpool The Mauricio Pochettino era got off to the worst possible start as Manchester United got thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card changed the complexion of the game completely. It was a naive challenge from the Frenchman, who has looked shaky all season. But the biggest issue on the night was Matthijs de Ligt. He lost his man for the red card and made error after error all night on what was his first Premier League start in almost a year. The Dutchman last played in the league back when Rúben Amorim was in charge. Since then, he has been sidelined with a back injury. Matthijs De Ligt should not have started Former head coach Michael Carrick did not feel the ex-Ajax ace was ready to step up, but Pochettino felt otherwise. And the decision backfired spectacularly. Away at Anfield against a rampaging Liverpool, the new head coach should have gone for the experienced Harry Maguire , who did eventually come on after Yoro’s red card. De Ligt looked like he had lost a yard of pace and could not turn on the ball as quickly, and he was rusty with his passing as well. The damning defeat will show the new boss exactly what a gargantuan task he has on his hands, with the Red Devils languishing in 19th place in the table. Pochettino has a huge task on his hands The action is relentless, with a midweek game coming up against Sporting CP in the Champions League. So time on the training pitch will be limited. The performance on the night was a reminder of how badly INEOS have let standards slip this season. It was clear for all to see that the team needed reinforcements at the back in the summer, but the co-owners opted to ignore it and revamp only the midfield. With relegation a very real possibility, INEOS must spend in January to help the new head coach. Otherwise, things could get murky very soon. Feature image Michael Regan via Getty Images

top.title: Kansas City Crowned Champions as Spirit Suffer Third Straight NWSL Final Defeat
top.description: Amber Searls-Imagn Images The Kansas City Current finally broke through to win their first NWSL championship on Saturday night, handing the Washington Spirit a crushing third consecutive loss in the league final. The game ended 2-1 at Audi Field, a result that feels like a perfect twist of fate for a Spirit team that plays on its home turf but keeps falling short. Vanessa DiBernardo scored a rare Olimpico goal from a corner kick to give Kansas City the lead, showcasing the veteran’s class. The Spirit’s Trinity Rodman managed to score a header one minute later, but it was too little, too late for a team that has now lost three straight finals. A Veteran’s Moment to Shine Vanessa DiBernardo earned the game’s MVP award , a fitting honor for a player who waited twelve years for this specific moment. She returned from maternity leave in July and had previously lost two finals with the Chicago Red Stars before joining Kansas City. Her teammates chanted “MomVP” as she accepted the award, a sweet nod to her journey and her role in the squad. Her goal briefly made her the oldest goalscorer in NWSL Championship history until Debinha, who is 35, took the record with her own late strike. This win marks a key turnaround for a franchise that struggled in the playoffs last year as the top seed. Washington’s Heartbreak Continues The Washington Spirit now holds the unwanted record of losing three straight finals, a streak that is hard to watch for any fan. The game was rough and full of fouls, with both teams combining for 19 fouls in the first half alone. No single half of an NWSL Championship has seen a higher count than the figure reported by ESPN Global Research. Just five minutes into the game, Rodman suffered an apparent left shoulder injury after a challenge from Kansas City defender Laney Rouse. She returned after two minutes of treatment, but the physical toll of the match seemed to weigh on the Spirit as they pushed for an equalizer. The Current secured the title by holding on in the final moments even as the Spirit endured another painful night at home. Kansas City is now the seventh franchise to win the NWSL Championship, joining a list that includes the Western New York Flash and North Carolina Courage.

top.title: Jack Nicklaus had plans for historic Florida municipal golf course. What happened?
top.description: For all its history, affordability and prime location along the Intracoastal Waterway, Lake Worth Beach Golf Club has a stubborn problem: water. “It just gets flooded and it’s terrible,” 18-time major champion Jack Nicklaus said. This fall, the nearly century-old municipal course has once again been battered by flooding. While the course has been open for play in recent weeks, much of it is sodden and muddy, even causing some drives in the fairway to plug into the ground. Some areas have suffered significant damage from apparent golf-cart traffic, while sections along the Intracoastal bear scars left by receding water. The course, like many in the county, closed Thursday, Nov. 19 amid more heavy rainfall and flooding. Nicklaus, who was honored as part of an American Free Enterprise event at Palm Beach Atlantic in West Palm Beach on Nov. 17, has become one of the sport’s most acclaimed golf-course designers. He has personally designed 325 courses and remains active in establishing "Nicklaus Design." The golf icon was involved in recent talks to redesign the popular public course in downtown Lake Worth Beach. The talks were part of a larger redevelopment proposal that also included hotel development across the Intracoastal, but the proposal did not move forward, according to Nicklaus. The golf course was part of the plan. I’m interested in helping out anywhere that wants help. “It’s a well-located piece of property,” Nicklaus added. “That could become a nice golf course. Right now, it just gets flooded and it’s terrible. The city has got to want to do it. If they don’t want to do it, there’s nothing I can do to help.” Lake Worth Beach mayor Betty Resch said the "Golden Bear" proposal ultimately was out of step with city residents. "His project was not just about the golf course, it would have completely changed the nature of our beachfront, taking it over with a huge hotel and convention center," Resch said. "Our people treasure the Old Florida feel of our city. We are the genuine thing, and hold that fact close to our hearts." The challenges presented by water, whether falling from the sky or rising from the Intracoastal, aren't new or lost on the longtime city resident-turned-politician. nigeria.title: Iran unveils new missile launcher as commanders issue warning to US
nigeria.description: Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher as senior military commanders touted the Islamic republic’s capabilities in defiant messages to the United States. “A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time,” Iranian state television reported on Saturday. State television broadcast footage of Revolutionary Guards chief Ahmad Vahidi and the head of the Guards’ aerospace forces, Majid Mousavi, touring an underground missile base. The two commanders were shown riding atop a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment. “The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation,” said Vahidi, whose Revolutionary Guards form the ideological arm of Iran’s military. “Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy,” said Mousavi. The unveiling comes months into the Middle East war, which broke out on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the conflict. During the war’s most intense phase, US-Israeli strikes targeted Iran’s missile capabilities and again hit its nuclear sites, though the extent of the damage remains unclear. nigeria.title: Climate deal collapses in chaotic end to COP31
nigeria.description: The COP31 climate talks ended in failure Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit stretched into record overtime in Turkey. The final agreement was dramatically rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit which ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at COP31, expressed deep dismay as the talks broke down. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. “Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters. More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks. – ‘Greenwash’ – Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory” as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal. “We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency. “And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.” Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record. – Falling short – The outcome revived memories of the failed Copenhagen summit of 2009 and raised fresh doubts about the effectiveness of climate diplomacy. “It certainly fell short today,” said UN climate chief Simon Stiell, describing progress over the marathon fortnight of negotiations in Antalya as “limited”. “The world cannot afford a repeat.” Frustrated by the inertia, countries are pushing ahead outside the COP process. nigeria.title: FG orders probe into deadly Bayelsa boat accident
nigeria.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has ordered an immediate investigation into the boat accident that claimed several lives in Bayelsa State, warning that it would no longer tolerate avoidable safety violations on the nation’s waterways. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, gave the directive to the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA), asking it to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and submit its findings to him. The mishap occurred on Friday, November 20, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Special Adviser, Dr Bolaji Akinola, Oyetola also directed NIWA to work with relevant government agencies and the Bayelsa State Government to ensure a transparent and comprehensive investigation. The minister described the loss of lives as worrisome and unacceptable, expressing concern over reports that passengers involved in the accident were not wearing life jackets. He also raised concerns over the alleged absence of a passenger manifest, stressing that proper documentation of passengers was a critical safety requirement that must be strictly enforced. “Safety lapses on our waterways are no longer acceptable. The Federal Government will not fold its arms and watch its citizens perish on the waterways. We must get to the root of this tragedy and ensure that those responsible for enforcing safety regulations do their jobs,” he said. Oyetola recalled that he visited Bayelsa State on May 2, 2025, where he distributed 3,500 life jackets to water transport users as part of efforts to improve safety on the waterways. He also renewed his call on state governments to gradually phase out wooden boats and replace them with safer and more durable fibreglass or fibre-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation. The minister disclosed that he had contacted Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, to commiserate with him, the state government and families of the victims. He sympathised with the bereaved families and prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died in the accident, while urging stakeholders to work together to prevent a recurrence. nigeria.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has commenced construction of a new road linking Bende Road through the Umuahia Post Office Tower and railway crossing to First Bank/Akanu Ibiam Road, with completion targeted before Christmas. The project, being executed by the Umuahia Capital Development Authority (UCDA), is designed to provide an alternative traffic corridor, ease congestion around Government House and Isigate, and improve connectivity within the state capital. The General Manager of UCDA, Engr. Kingsley Agomoh, who conducted journalists round the project site, said the road would allow motorists coming from Bende and Ikot Ekpene roads to connect to Abia Line, Aguiyi Ironsi Boulevard, Abia Express Tower and Onuimo Road without passing through the Government House axis. He said the project would significantly reduce traffic pressure on major roads, stimulate economic activities and improve the aesthetics of Umuahia. ” If you are coming from Bende Road, you pass through the Post Office Tower, cross the railway station and connect to First Bank, Ridge Club and Abia Line without going through the Government House axis,” Agomoh said. He explained that the project was part of Otti’s broader urban renewal programme, adding that the governor had also directed the relocation of Umuahia Railway Station to the Nnennaya Oti Bus Terminal. According to him, the state government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Nigerian Railway Corporation to facilitate the construction of the access road across the railway corridor. Agomoh also disclosed that another road linking First Bank to the Keystone, Sterling and FCMB bank areas would be reopened and reconstructed to provide motorists, particularly those coming from the Federal Medical Centre, Umuahia, with a shorter alternative route. He said the road, which had been encroached upon by adjoining property owners, was being reclaimed to restore access and ease movement within the commercial district. Describing the railway-crossing road as a signature project of the Otti administration, Agomoh said the governor’s urban renewal drive was repositioning Umuahia for increased economic activities and orderly development. nigeria.title: I didn’t politicise it — Gov Yusuf narrates how wife left Kano Govt House
nigeria.description: Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has broken his silence on his marital crisis with wife, Zainab, recounting how she allegedly left the Government House and later initiated divorce proceedings against him in Abuja. The governor, in an interview with BBC Hausa aired on Sunday, said he had remained quiet despite developments in the marriage, which he said had lasted about two decades and produced children. Yusuf said Zainab, a niece of his former political ally, Rabiu Kwankwaso, was previously married before they got together. He recalled that their relationship eventually deteriorated, leading to her departure from the Government House, an experience he said he endured without publicly discussing the matter. “Many things happened, to the point where her belongings were packed and she was taken away from my house, and through it all, I remained patient and did not speak out,” Yusuf said. He said he had tried to reassure their children that their mother would return, but was subsequently taken aback when the matter ended up in court. The governor said he was particularly surprised that the divorce suit was filed in Abuja rather than Kano. “Suddenly, she dragged me to court, a court in Abuja, not even in Kano,” he said. Yusuf described the development as distressing, adding that he had information about the circumstances surrounding his wife’s departure but would not publicly disclose the details. Asked whether he was using the family dispute for political purposes, the governor denied bringing politics into the matter, questioning how anyone in a similar situation would react. “I am not the one who politicised it. If this was done to you, how would you feel?” he asked. He further lamented that his wife’s belongings were removed and she was taken to another residence without his knowledge, before he learnt that she had instituted legal proceedings against him. The marital dispute is before the Upper Area Court in the Gudu District of Abuja, where the divorce case, marked CV/97/26, was adjourned until December 15. The adjournment followed a request by Kano Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, who represented Yusuf, for more time to brief the governor on the court proceedings. The crisis has drawn political attention because of Yusuf’s relationship with Kwankwaso, who played a significant role in his political rise. Their relationship reportedly deteriorated after Yusuf defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party to the All Progressives Congress in January 2026, while Kwankwaso later joined the New Nigeria Democratic Congress. nigeria.title: Barcelona fight back from two goals down to beat Villarreal, extend La Liga lead
nigeria.description: Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga. Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first half penalty. However the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory. Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them the three points. Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October. “We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I’ll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn’t happen again,” Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN. “Against a team like this you can’t always turn things around from two down.” The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute. Fermin Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance to send the visitors ahead. Two minutes later Villarreal doubled their advantage when Tani Oluwaseyi, another Canadian, broke in down the left flank and smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net. Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. Yamal took it himself but dragged his effort against the post and wide. The winger tried to make amends with a burst inside from the wing before half-time but Peter Gulacsi palmed away his cross-shot and the goalkeeper and his defence combined to thwart Eric Garcia on the follow up. – Quickfire treble – Barcelona came out invigorated in the second half and quickly dragged themselves back into the match. Pedri shot wide and Gulacsi saved from Lopez’s low effort before Martin found the net in the 57th minute. Pedri crossed the ball in from the left for the defender to head home. Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow. A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro. Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily. Navarro was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time as Villarreal, ninth, left frustrated. “The (first Barca) goal psychologically killed us, they gained confidence, a couple of minutes later they equalised and from there it’s a lot more difficult,” Comesana told DAZN. nigeria.title: Bayern’s Musiala suffered another seizure this week
nigeria.description: Bayern Munich and Germany midfielder Jamal Musiala suffered another previously undisclosed seizure this week, according to information received by AFP subsidiary SID on Sunday. The incident, which is categorised by a brief and temporary loss of consciousness or awareness, occurred at training on Monday. Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season with the 23-year-old later revealing he had a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Monday’s incident was the second since Musiala’s announcement, with the player reportedly adjusting his medication to properly treat the condition while continuing to play. News of the incident comes as Bayern have faced criticism from footballers’ union FIFPRO for a “coordinated campaign” to pressure the Germany international to renegotiate his 2025-extended contract. “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. On Friday, Bayern supervisory board member and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the midfielder may need to take a pay cut if he cannot recapture his old form. “Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” Rummenigge said. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.” The post Bayern’s Musiala suffered another seizure this week appeared first on Vanguard News .

entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. Qualifying travellers with connections of at least 20 hours and up to seven days may receive complimentary hotel accommodation. Under the standard programme, eligible Economy Class passengers can receive one night in a four-star hotel, while Business Class passengers may receive two nights in a five-star or boutique hotel. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. sports.title: Own goal helps Brighton & Hove Albion record victory at Everton
sports.description: Own goal helps Brighton & Hove Albion record victory at Everton A Maz Pacheco own goal helped Brighton & Hove Albion to record a 1-0 victory over Everton at Goodison Park on Sunday afternoon. Pacheco put through her own net after just six minutes as the visitors ended the second block of matches with a win. Olivia García created an early chance for Brighton & Hove Albion. She passed the ball to captain Maisie Symonds, but she sent her effort wide. Pacheco then netted an own goal when her back-pass deceived both Rion Ishikawa and Courtney Brosnan and the ball rolled into the goal. Brighton & Hove Albion searched for a second goal. A ball was played through by Lily Murphy towards Kiko Seike, but her touch wasn’t enough and it was caught well by Brosnan. Fran Kirby then played the ball to Seike, but Ishikawa timed her run perfectly and intercepted the ball. Ornella Vignola almost found an equaliser for Everton. She attempted to whip the ball towards the far corner, but her shot went just wide. Hannah Blundell was then in on goal, but her shot was saved by Chiamaka Nnadozie. Jutta Rantala was next to have a chance in the box, but her effort was blocked. Brighton & Hove Albion went close when Marisa Olislagers struck the ball from range, but Brosnan got her finger tips to it as the game ended 1-0 in The Seagulls’ favour. This afternoon’s result sees Brighton & Hove Albion go to seventh place in the Barclays Women’s Super League table while Everton drop to 11th.

sports.title: Hornets Considering Paying Too High A Price For Zion Williamson Trade
sports.description: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets sit at 4-11 and need a spark, but a proposed trade for Zion Williamson looks like a terrible mistake. The team is desperate for offense after a 111-97 loss in Atlanta on Friday night, yet the cost to get the Pelicans star is simply too high. The Cost of Four Draft Picks The front office pitched the LaMelo deal as a move toward the future, yet this new proposal burns that future for a player with a shaky track record. Yahoo Sports reports that a complete cost analysis indicates paying such a price makes very little sense. Health Concerns and Salary Traps Availability remains the single biggest question mark for any team acquiring the 26-year-old forward. The risk remains massive even though clauses based on games played protect his $42.17 million salary for this season and his $44.89 million deal for 2027-28. Over the course of seven seasons, Williamson has played over just 60 games on only three occasions. The consensus is that he is unable to stay healthy. On the Hoop Collective podcast, ESPN’s Tim MacMahon reported that the Pelicans are unlikely to receive a blockbuster price. “And kind of the consensus that I’ve gotten is, hey, there will be interest in Zion, but there’s not going to be like a blockbuster type of return,” McMahon said. sports.title: Michigan Takes Down UCLA, Ready for Ohio State
sports.description: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham reacts to a play against UCLA during the second half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Michigan football finally found its footing after a hard-fought win over UCLA . The Wolverines secured a spot in a bowl game with an 18-16 victory in triple overtime. This win at The Big House improved the team’s record to 6-5. But head coach Kyle Whittingham is not looking back at the celebration. His mind is already fixed on the next big challenge. The coaching staff knows the season is far from over. There is only one regular-season game left on the schedule. That final matchup is the annual rivalry against Ohio State. Whittingham knows the stakes are high as the team heads to Columbus. He wants his players to carry the momentum from Saturday forward. Facing a Hostile Road Trip Whittingham has never played inside Ohio Stadium, known as The Shoe. He admits he cannot fully picture the noise until he gets there. “I can envision it. I’ve never been in the Shoe, never played in that stadium,” Whittingham said. Whittingham has faced Ohio State before in a major bowl game. His Utah team met the Buckeyes in the 2022 Rose Bowl, losing a 48-45 shootout. “We did play Ohio State in the Rose Bowl 5 years ago, 4 years ago, so we’ve had a taste of that, and they were … we know they’re a very good football team, very talented,” he added. The coach expects the crowd in Columbus to be loud and angry. He mentioned that Ohio State lost a recent game in Nebraska. “I guess they got beat today in Nebraska, but I think the environment I’m anticipating to be very hostile,” he said. Whittingham has faced tough crowds in his long career. He is not sure if this one will be the worst he has seen, but he is ready to find out. The team must handle the pressure without breaking. Questions About the Coach’s Future While the team celebrates a bowl berth, some fans worry about Whittingham’s job. The season started with high hopes and a roster full of talent. Instead, the team struggled to find a rhythm for most of the year. Insiders at The Athletic reported that some parents of players may have mixed emotions; one said he can “get the program on track if given enough time.” Critics point to specific issues that hurt the team this year. According to The Athletic’s Bruce Feldman and Austin Meek, the offense utilized a “scheme that wasn’t built for the Big Ten.” They also noted a “CEO-style” approach that kept Whittingham too far from the field. Dan Wetzel on the Paul Finebaum Show argued that Whittingham’s legacy is safe despite this year. “Kyle Whittingham as a coach, his legacy is mostly secured. This just, for whatever reason, didn’t gel,” Wetzel stated. The final test will come next week in Ohio. Michigan heads to Columbus for its annual rivalry matchup against Ohio State on November 28. The Wolverines will look to carry the momentum from their win over UCLA into one of the season’s biggest challenges.

The 21-year-old starlet proved to be the Merengues’ saviour once again in his debut season, chipping in with the 85th-minute winner as the team secured a comeback 2-1 victory. Fernando Sanz bats for more prominent role for Espi Espi continues to make vital contributions despite having played very limited minutes at the Santiago Bernabeu, given that Kylian Mbappe is the undisputed starter at centre-forward. And, echoing the sentiments of another former Real Madrid star Santi Canizares , Sanz has asked for the young striker to be given a greater role by Jose Mourinho. Real Madrid’s match-winner. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Analysing the team’s performance on the night, the ex-defender said on Radio MARCA : “A lackluster performance from Real Madrid, the kind of game we saw at the beginning of the season that drove us to despair, but very positive in the introduction of Vinicius and, above all, in the introduction of Espi.” Moving on to Espi, he added: “He’s a player who, after today’s performance, deserves many more minutes than he’s getting. I think he’s a player who could score a lot of goals for Real Madrid, and in fact, he will.” Espi’s attitude embodies what Real Madrid supporters value Beyond the winning goal, Sanz was particularly impressed by Espi’s willingness to compete for every ball. He highlighted a determined challenge during a corner as an example of the qualities that make the striker appealing to the Bernabeu crowd. Making a big impact off the bench. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) “That fighting spirit, that sacrifice, that sense of honor, that teamwork, that humility – I think those are the characteristics of a Real Madrid player,” he explained. Continuing, Sanz added: “It’s not about being a virtuoso, a phenomenon, but that’s what Real Madrid fans like. “That fighting spirit, that sense of honour, that’s what Madrid fans love, especially in the final minutes, that heroic effort, that fight, that’s what a Real Madrid fan loves most.” So far in his debut season at Real Madrid, Espi has played only 62 minutes across 12 matches, but has chipped in with four goals.

sports.title: Kansas City Crowned Champions as Spirit Suffer Third Straight NWSL Final Defeat
sports.description: Amber Searls-Imagn Images The Kansas City Current finally broke through to win their first NWSL championship on Saturday night, handing the Washington Spirit a crushing third consecutive loss in the league final. The game ended 2-1 at Audi Field, a result that feels like a perfect twist of fate for a Spirit team that plays on its home turf but keeps falling short. Vanessa DiBernardo scored a rare Olimpico goal from a corner kick to give Kansas City the lead, showcasing the veteran’s class. The Spirit’s Trinity Rodman managed to score a header one minute later, but it was too little, too late for a team that has now lost three straight finals. A Veteran’s Moment to Shine Vanessa DiBernardo earned the game’s MVP award , a fitting honor for a player who waited twelve years for this specific moment. She returned from maternity leave in July and had previously lost two finals with the Chicago Red Stars before joining Kansas City. Her teammates chanted “MomVP” as she accepted the award, a sweet nod to her journey and her role in the squad. Her goal briefly made her the oldest goalscorer in NWSL Championship history until Debinha, who is 35, took the record with her own late strike. This win marks a key turnaround for a franchise that struggled in the playoffs last year as the top seed. Washington’s Heartbreak Continues The Washington Spirit now holds the unwanted record of losing three straight finals, a streak that is hard to watch for any fan. The game was rough and full of fouls, with both teams combining for 19 fouls in the first half alone. No single half of an NWSL Championship has seen a higher count than the figure reported by ESPN Global Research. Just five minutes into the game, Rodman suffered an apparent left shoulder injury after a challenge from Kansas City defender Laney Rouse. She returned after two minutes of treatment, but the physical toll of the match seemed to weigh on the Spirit as they pushed for an equalizer. The Current secured the title by holding on in the final moments even as the Spirit endured another painful night at home. Kansas City is now the seventh franchise to win the NWSL Championship, joining a list that includes the Western New York Flash and North Carolina Courage.

sports.title: Jack Nicklaus had plans for historic Florida municipal golf course. What happened?
sports.description: For all its history, affordability and prime location along the Intracoastal Waterway, Lake Worth Beach Golf Club has a stubborn problem: water. “It just gets flooded and it’s terrible,” 18-time major champion Jack Nicklaus said. This fall, the nearly century-old municipal course has once again been battered by flooding. While the course has been open for play in recent weeks, much of it is sodden and muddy, even causing some drives in the fairway to plug into the ground. Some areas have suffered significant damage from apparent golf-cart traffic, while sections along the Intracoastal bear scars left by receding water. The course, like many in the county, closed Thursday, Nov. 19 amid more heavy rainfall and flooding. Nicklaus, who was honored as part of an American Free Enterprise event at Palm Beach Atlantic in West Palm Beach on Nov. 17, has become one of the sport’s most acclaimed golf-course designers. He has personally designed 325 courses and remains active in establishing "Nicklaus Design." The golf icon was involved in recent talks to redesign the popular public course in downtown Lake Worth Beach. The talks were part of a larger redevelopment proposal that also included hotel development across the Intracoastal, but the proposal did not move forward, according to Nicklaus. More coverage: Lake Worth Beach's economy could get boost with Nicklaus golf course, Hyatt hotels “We looked at it a while back,” Nicklaus said. “The city decided not to go through with the plans the developer proposed. The golf course was part of the plan. I’m interested in helping out anywhere that wants help. “It’s a well-located piece of property,” Nicklaus added. “That could become a nice golf course. Right now, it just gets flooded and it’s terrible. The city has got to want to do it. If they don’t want to do it, there’s nothing I can do to help.” Lake Worth Beach mayor Betty Resch said the "Golden Bear" proposal ultimately was out of step with city residents. "His project was not just about the golf course, it would have completely changed the nature of our beachfront, taking it over with a huge hotel and convention center," Resch said. "Our people treasure the Old Florida feel of our city. We are the genuine thing, and hold that fact close to our hearts." The challenges presented by water, whether falling from the sky or rising from the Intracoastal, aren't new or lost on the longtime city resident-turned-politician. "Yes, the golf course is in an incredible spot, and yes it does flood with king tides, major rain events and the rising sea level," Resch said. "It's a challenge that the city will have to meet, but not at the expense of our character. And let's not dismiss the fact that it is a functioning, unique course, enjoyed by many and extensively played." sports.description: UAlbany head coach Tom Perkovich during a game against Delaware State University on Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026, at Casey Stadium in Albany, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) ALBANY - The University at Albany football team, which won only two games a year ago, is going to the Football Championship Subdivision playoffs. The Great Danes (8-4) were selected as an at-large team when the 24-team field was announced on Sunday on ESPNU. UAlbany will play at 12th-seeded Lehigh (10-2) on Saturday in Bethlehem, Pa. UAlbany, which finished tied for second in the Coastal Athletic Association with a 6-2 league record, makes its first appearance in the postseason since reaching the FCS semifinals for the first time in program history in 2023. The Great Danes slipped to a 2-10 record last season. However, first-year coach Tom Perkovich turned the program around this season after coming from Division III Susquehanna. The winner of UAlbany-Lehigh will play No. 5 Stephen F. Austin (11-1) on Dec. 5 in Texas in a second-round game. The Great Danes were one of the last four teams in, while CAA rival Bryant was one of the first three teams out, according to the ESPNU broadcast. Bryant, which finished tied for second with UAlbany in the CAA, beat the Great Danes 31-7 in Smithfield, R.I. two weeks ago. The Great Danes did have an overall strength of schedule - based on opponents' combined winning percentage - that was significantly higher than Bryant's. sports.title: Pochettino debut ends in disaster as Man United lose 4-0 at Liverpool
sports.description: Pochettino debut ends in disaster as Man United lose 4-0 at Liverpool Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge of Manchester United ended in disaster after a 4-0 humiliation at Liverpool. Optimism had greeted Pochettino’s appointment as Michael Carrick’s successor during the international break, but the Argentine faces a huge task to turn things around at a struggling side. A nightmare start saw Manchester United reduced to 10 men inside eight minutes when Leny Yoro bundled over Alexander Isak, with the incident deemed a clear goalscoring opportunity. Things went from bad to worse when Dominik Szoboszlai blasted in the resulting free-kick, before an acrobatic effort from Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead three minutes later Pochettino attempted shore things up by replacing Bryan Mbeumo with Harry Maguire, reverting to a back-five system. The change of shape stopped the bleeding until half-time, but Liverpool continued to exploit space going forward after the break. A rapid counter-attack saw the Reds make it 3-0 on 66 minutes, as Bradley Barcola burst away to set up Rio Ngumoha. A fourth concluded a fine afternoon for Liverpool, as a neat move saw Florian Wirtz and Victor Munoz exchange passes, before the latter slammed home. The result leaves Manchester United 19th in the Premier League table, and with the worst defensive record in Europe’s top five leagues in all competitions. In contrast, Liverpool secured their best win of Andoni Iraola’s reign so far and move within a point of third-place Manchester City. sports.title: Dylan Larkin Gives Up Over 7 Figures Waiting for Red Wings Trade
sports.description: Dylan Larkin Red Wings Getty Former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin has given up over seven figures in forfeited salary while he awaits a trade. Larkin asked the Red Wings for a trade in the summer, but the team held onto him, and he came to training camp with the team. After playing in a handful of games with Detroit, he decided to step away from the team on October 29. He has been suspended since then and is losing $41,000 per day in forfeited salary. Dylan Larkin Has Given Up $1 Million in Salary On Sunday, Larkin’s forfeited salary topped the $1 million mark, per Helene St. James of the Detroit Free Press. “The former Detroit Red Wings captain now has topped $1 million in forfeited salary since he had his agent inform the team he ‘no longer wants to be a Red Wing’ on Oct. 29, at which point the Wings changed his status to suspended without pay. Larkin, from Waterford, is forfeiting just north of $41,000 a day. That Larkin would leave so much money on the table – true, his career earnings already top $66 million, not bad for a 30-year-old – speaks to resolve in wanting what he asked for shortly after last season ended in April: A trade away from his hometown NHL team, the one that drafted him No. 15 in 2014, and of which he served as captain from January 2021 until this past offseason,” St. James wrote. When Will the Red Wings Trade Dylan Larkin? The Red Wings seem to be wanting to wait for the perfect trade to send Larkin away . As of yet, they have not gotten the trade package that they want to deal him, but as the clock continues to tick, the team really needs to think about dealing their top trade asset and stop being so picky with what sort of trade offers they get back, as Larkin sitting on the sidelines isn’t good for anyone. The NHL trade deadline is on March 1, so the Red Wings still have a lot of time left, but for the sake of both the player and the team, it would be better to trade him ASAP. sports.title: 'Sacked in the morning' chants start early for Man Utd boss Pochettino
sports.description: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Manchester United at the Anfield. (is associated with: «'Sacked in the morning' chants start early for Man Utd boss Pochettino») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa The job of Manchester United head coach has become something of a poisoned chalice for a succession of managers but even new boss Mauricio Pochettino could not have expected to have been taunted with jokes about him being sacked. His reign began in humiliating fashion after an early red card and two goals led to the Kop at Anfield chanting “sacked in the morning” just 13 minutes into the Argentinian’s first game. United’s all-time great boss Sir Alex Ferguson had a seat in the directors’ box alongside the actor and fan James Nesbitt – in Liverpool recording a new Poirot television show – and it was more a case of boiling blood than ‘Cold Feet’ at Anfield. Ferguson had shared a pre-match joke with fellow Scot and long-time Liverpool rival Kenny Dalglish about their choice of chocolate but that was about as funny as it got for the 84-year-old. There were also some stony faces from chief executive officer Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, sat immediately in front of Ferguson, after a shambolic start for the new head coach. Chants of “going down with the City” when the third goal went in – followed by “you’re not famous any more” and “Poch is at the wheel” – will only have made the trip back along the M62 more uncomfortable.

technology.title: As cars go digital, US consumers pay an extra $12 billion a year for repairs
technology.description: The computerization of cars comes at a price to US consumers, according to the Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), which says that software fees and other charges faced by mechanics push up garage costs. An investigation by the non-profit consumer group estimates that car repair costs for Americans have been inflated by $12 billion each year, as vehicles integrate more computerized functions. Its report, Closing Shop , is available online. To find a failed sensor, release an electronic parking brake, or perform diagnostics, a technician has to first connect a laptop or tablet to the vehicle. To so this, the repair shop has to have the right software tools, and that means paying the vehicle manufacturer subscription charges and other fees, in order to get the information they need to complete the job. If smaller independent repair shops can’t afford all the necessary software or subscriptions, they may be forced to steer customers to authorized dealerships for some fixes – about one in five jobs – and this allows the latter to charge more. PIRG claims that drivers pay for this through their insurance premiums, even if they never need to get their car fixed, because higher repair costs mean higher insurance claims. It says the price of auto insurance has risen three times as fast as the rest of the US economy since 2012. Even if mechanics do choose to pay for the software, they spend an estimated collective 83 million hours a year buying, downloading, logging in, and waiting. At typical repair rates, that adds up to $12 billion. A separate report from the PIRG Education Fund claims that a two-tiered repair model now exists, where independent sites conduct repairs with less information, less powerful diagnostic tools, and higher associated costs than the authorized dealerships. science.title: SpaceX sends classified US spy satellites to orbit in early-morning launch from California coast (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the NROL-136 mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office from California on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the U.S. Space Force , and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 is the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend.
